text:
anya.dev: quick check — running into weird abort + retry interactions when streaming from SDKs. node -> our hosted API: AbortController.abort() seems to close socket, but server still processes remainder and sometimes retries kick in. Anyone else?

sam: saw this yesterday. python async client: calling cancel() on the stream coroutine leaves server hanging for ~30s before connection fully closes. flakey in load tests. :eyes:

mike_r: we instrumented go client too — context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2s) cancels, but grpc/http2 connections sometimes keep the server-side handler alive until the request body EOF. race with retry layer.

nisha: important detail — is the retry happening in the client lib or at the infra layer? we have both (SDK automatic retries + gateway fallback).

anya.dev: in our repro it was SDK retry. Sequence: client starts streaming, aborts mid-stream (user cancels), SDK schedules a retry because upstream returned 5xx on final chunk, then the new attempt races with lingering server work.

sam: pasted minimal Node repro: 
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const r = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body: stream, signal: ac.signal });
// later
ac.abort(); // client aborts stream
```
observed behavior: socket closes but server logs show handler still running until timeout.

mike_r: Go snippet: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
client.Do(req)
```
server sees ctx.Done() but goroutine blocks on reading full body sometimes.

nisha: hypothesis — kernel TCP state and http/2 flow control lead to server not seeing EOF immediately. also if SDK retries, the second request reuses connection and confuses server-side read loop.

anya.dev: open question: what should SDK semantics be for cancel during streaming? options: 1) abort and never retry, 2) abort but allow retry only if no bytes were sent, 3) best-effort half-close and surface clearer error to app.

sam: my vote: default to "no automatic retry on client-initiated abort". If user explicitly sets retry and idempotency, we can allow it. This avoids surprise duplicate processing.

mike_r: +1. for Go SDK we can make context cancellation map to an explicit non-retriable error type so retry layer drops it. easy change.

nisha: Node + Python: mapping AbortSignal to a non-retriable error is doable. need tests for streaming to ensure we don't regress.

ci-bot: build #stream-timeouts (PR 4821) — integration tests: stream-abort-on-client, expected non-retriable; result: FAILED (flaky). logs: https://ci/redwood/4821/logs

anya.dev: plan proposal:
- SDKs: treat client-initiated cancel as non-retriable. throw error subclass like `AbortError` that retry policy honors.
- Docs: add section "abort vs timeout vs server error" + examples for Node/Go/Python.
- Tests: new integration test that aborts mid-stream and asserts no second request received.

sam: also add an escape hatch: opt-in retry-on-abort for idempotent endpoints with explicit flag. keep default safe.

mike_r: I'll make a small Go PR to change retry policy mapping and add a unit test. cc @nisha for node/python changes.

nisha: I'll open node PR after lunch. quick change: map AbortSignal to retryPolicy.NO_RETRY and update docs. will add example using `controller.abort()` with explanation.

anya.dev: nice. can we also add a note about server-side read timeouts? suggest adding a short server read deadline for streaming endpoints so long-running leftover goroutines don't pile up.

mike_r: will add server read deadline by default (configurable). reduces resource leaks.

sam: i'll add a small e2e test in the sdk test harness to simulate kernel-level delays (tcp blackhole) so we catch racey EOF handling.

anya.dev: thanks team. i'll draft the doc blurb and link PRs here. calling this a crack at alignment — meeting not needed unless blockers. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: note: flake ticket created (#INF-2992) for follow-up on intermittent failures.

nisha: ping me here when PRs are up, i'll review the node change first.

anya.dev: pinged. moving to follow-up board.
